q: Diffraction is defined as the bending of waves around the corners of an obstacle (or) through an aperture into the region of geometrical ____ of the obstacle (or) aperture.
e: Diffraction is bending around an obstacle or through an aperture into the geometrical shadow. It is obvious when the opening is comparable to the wavelength, not when the hole is huge. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: Diffraction is defined as the ____ of waves around the corners of an obstacle (or) through an aperture.
e: Diffraction is bending around an obstacle or through an aperture into the geometrical shadow. It is obvious when the opening is comparable to the wavelength, not when the hole is huge. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition. Intensity does not set the bend; wavelength versus size does.

q: The amount of bending depends on the wavelength of light relative to the ____ of the aperture.
e: Wavelength sets fringe spacing, diffraction angles and colour order on a grating. Longer lambda, larger angle in d sin theta = m lambda, so red sits farther out than violet. Monochromatic work uses one lambda so patterns do not smear. Aperture is the circular hole light goes through.

q: If the aperture is much larger than the wavelength of light, the bending will be almost ____.
e: Wavelength sets fringe spacing, diffraction angles and colour order on a grating. Longer lambda, larger angle in d sin theta = m lambda, so red sits farther out than violet. Monochromatic work uses one lambda so patterns do not smear. f-number is focal length divided by that diameter.

q: Light waves diffract around objects and create bright and dark ____.
e: Fringe width is the gap between neighbouring bright fringes, or neighbouring dark ones. In Young's setup it is lambda D over d. It depends on wavelength; red fringes sit farther apart than violet. A different driver in place of Light would describe a different law.

q: A very simple demonstration of light diffraction can be conducted by placing the sharp edges of a razor blade in front of intense blue light from a ____ source.
e: Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and a mirror cavity; the beam is coherent and monochromatic. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: There are two main classes of diffraction, which are known as Fresnel diffraction and ____ diffraction.
e: Fresnel diffraction keeps source and screen at finite distance from the obstacle, so the wavefront is curved. Fraunhofer is the infinite-distance, plane-wavefront limit. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: Fresnel diffraction: The source of light and the screen are at a ____ distance from the obstacle causing the diffraction.
e: Fresnel diffraction keeps source and screen at finite distance from the obstacle, so the wavefront is curved. Fraunhofer is the infinite-distance, plane-wavefront limit. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition. Those two classes are the split in this chapter.

q: Fraunhofer diffraction: There is an ____ distance between the source and the screen from the obstacle.
e: Fraunhofer diffraction treats source and screen as infinitely far, giving plane wavefronts. Lenses often create that condition in the lab. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: The diffraction pattern consists of a bright central portion (the central ____).
e: A bright maximum needs constructive interference, integer path difference. On a grating, d sin theta = m lambda locates those maxima. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: These bright and dark fringes are created by ____ of diffracted light waves.
e: Interference is superposition of waves in the same medium, making bright and dark fringes. Sources must be coherent: same frequency and a steady phase difference. Young's two slits from one monochromatic parent wave are the classic setup. In Young's setup it is lambda D over d.

q: Each successive bright fringes becomes less ____ proceeding outward, away from the central maximum.
e: A bright maximum needs constructive interference, integer path difference. On a grating, d sin theta = m lambda locates those maxima. Half-integer path difference is a minimum. Fringe width is the gap between neighbouring bright fringes, or neighbouring dark ones.

q: The path difference between two waves from the centre and top edge of the slit is ____ and these two waves are exactly out of phase with one another.
e: Path difference is extra distance along the propagation direction. It is not a sideways gap. m lambda is in phase; (m+1/2) lambda is out of phase. Path difference between two waves from the cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: When they arrive at the screen, they interfere destructively and produces a dark fringe called the first ____.
e: A minimum is destructive interference. Single-slit minima sit at a sin theta = m lambda. Young's dark fringes are the half-integer path-difference case.

q: For the second minimum in single slit diffraction, the slit is divided into ____ parts.
e: Single-slit diffraction has a bright central maximum of width 2 lambda D / a, then alternating minima and weaker maxima. A wider slit narrows that central band. Reflection is a bounce; interference is two-wave addition.

q: Generally for the mth minimum, the condition is $a \sin\theta = $ ____.
e: A minimum is destructive interference. Single-slit minima sit at a sin theta = m lambda. Young's dark fringes are the half-integer path-difference case. Generally for the mth minimum the condition cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: The width of the central maximum depends on ____ of the slit.
e: A bright maximum needs constructive interference, integer path difference. On a grating, d sin theta = m lambda locates those maxima. Half-integer path difference is a minimum. A single slit spreads light into a wide central maximum of width 2 lambda D / a.

q: The narrower slit causes the ____ central maximum.
e: A bright maximum needs constructive interference, integer path difference. On a grating, d sin theta = m lambda locates those maxima. Half-integer path difference is a minimum. Two slits make Young's straight fringes.

q: The width of the central maximum is equal to 2 times the position of the first ____.
e: A minimum is destructive interference. Single-slit minima sit at a sin theta = m lambda. Young's dark fringes are the half-integer path-difference case. Half-integer path difference is a minimum.
